summary: Add exposedRectLeftMargin window property
description:
The bottom part content in fullscreen in most apps is not related to the content visible in widget state. The designer wants this bottom content to have a fixed width (even though the widget width differs from fullscreen width) and to look like it has a fixed X position (even though the X value of the app animates from 80px in widget states to 0px in fullscreen).

It could be solved by adding a window property ("exposedRectLeftMargin") so that the app bottom content can have a leftMargin of -exposedRectLeftMargin.

summary: Resolve our UI scalability story
description:
Right now there's a mix of Style.hspan()/vspan(), hardcoded pixels and pixel*scaleFactor (in instrument cluster) values in our code base.

neptune-ui inherited a scheme of dealing with different sizes from neptune-ui but it's following it half-heartedly. And that is hspan()/vspan() in conjunction with different conf files for different screen resolutions.

The UI design specs area made in plain pixels mostly, aimed specifically at 1080p displays in portrait (1920x1080).

We need to decide on what's our story in when it comes to graphical scalability. There's a use case I find really important and where Neptune Center Console window is sorely lacking which is:

Neptune Center Console should look good right out of the box in any display you run it on.

Neptune Instrument Cluster is good in that area as it already scales to fit the window it's run in.

Making a UI that is specific for a resolution makes it look like legacy code. Selecting different resolutions by selecting a different conf file, like in neptune-ui, is clunky and gives a bad out-of-the-box experience (see use case 1). There's a sad story here: https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/AUTOSUITE-192 that illustrates the point.

I think we must achieve one of those UI scalability modes:

A) Neptune fills the window it's run into by relayouting and scaling its content to match the window's resolution and aspect ratio.

B) Neptune fills the window it's run into by scaling its UI uniformly in both dimentions, keeping its original aspect ratio. The end result being letterboxing ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letterboxing_(filming])) if the display aspect ratio doesn't match Neptune's one. This is what Neptune's Instrument Cluster window is doing.

B is quite easy to achieve and lets the designer to still specify his UI designs in pixels for a 1080p display.

A requires much more though to be put on the UI design and might require some compromises on pixel-perfect transitions etc for the sake of flexibility and adaptability. But that leads to more widely useful and resilient UIs.

summary: `MusicBrowseListPanel.qml` clear out business logic
description:
`MusicBrowseListPanel.qml` and `MusicPlayQueuePanel.qml` contains logic to select the correct text. 

This applies to Delegate Item's imageSource, text and subText properties. The logic shall be either moved to a store or as these are methods attached to a delegate they could also move to a helper in the not yet existing "helpers" folder which should only contains JS files.

The logic behind this separation is that in the future we might want to move this code from JS to C++ for performance reasons. Also the UI logic shall be clean from business logic.

summary: Add LTR/RTL layout changes support for the internationalisation of Neptune UI
description:
As a next step for better internationalisation support, Neptune UI should support a LTR/RTL layout changes. No restart of the UI should be required to switch between LTR/RTL.

################### 

Some history FYI from the original task. The below results in multiple tasks which will be cloned from the original one:

Based on the discussion with Alistair and Alex at TU Detroit (June 2016), modified based on workshop at Berlin September 2016.

For demoing Qt's i18n features it would be nice if Neptune could do live language changes and LTR/RTL layout changes.
 * Need setting for the system language. Is this an OS setting or is there a separate UI setting taking into account whether on target or on PC development?
 * On System language change need to notify all the apps.
 * QML needs to be enhanced to have proper fix for language change. Volker has a patch that was rejected. Simon knows this is a problem and says that changes coming that makes this easier.
 * To make the notification propagation work we need an IPC mechanism.

A demo app has been built that is a starting point for demonstrating this feature. It does make the VKB follow the system language rather than having it's own inconvenient to use language cycle button. This feature should though be built into the system UI or an system settings app.

original_summary_sprint: System modal poups for applications
original_description_sprint:
Applications should be able to trigger system modal popups.

 

This is a multi-step (and hence multiple commits) task:
 # Rename NeptunePopup to PopupItem
 # Create an example in the sheets app making use of PopupItem
 # Create a new component called PopupWindow, which inherits from ApplicationManagerWindow (just like PrimaryWindow and SecondaryWindow). PopupWindow will have a window property called "windowType" whose value is "popup". system ui will take care of showing this window at the appropriate layer and of summing the blurred background behind it. There shall be an example in the sheets app making use of PopupWindow, alongside the existing PopupItem one. Both PopupItem and PopupWindow should be propertly documented, particularly regarding the difference between the two.

summary: Add UI controls by hardware keys in the cluster UI
description:
As a user, I want to have a navigation support for the UI. Currently the Neptune UI is a touch-only HMI. We still use a few keyboard shortcuts for development purposes. Some of those, like switching the content shown on cluster, are actually HMI actions and should be mapped to an actual device. The idea is to add support of a steering wheel used in games and use it in shows. A use of a standard PC keyboard should be retained for cases when no steering wheel is connected.

The following use cases have been identified for the initial implementation:
 # Use key on the wheel to switch the content in the center of the cluster UI between apps using this area (currently Maps and Media)
 # Be able to emulate right and left turn by another set of keys
 # Go forward and backward with arrow keys through the songs played by the Media Player
 # Document all used keys, which hardware is required, and how it is implemented in the UI code in a dedicated page of the docs, not just in the Overview page ([https://doc-snapshots.qt.io/neptune3ui/neptune3ui-overview.html])

summary: Unification of build and install steps
description:
Currently, in 5.12, only the Neptune docs explains steps how to build the key components: https://doc.qt.io/Neptune3UI/neptune3ui-build-run.html

A new commit with the new landing page mentions that steps on the landing page now as well, still the problem remains that QtIVI, appman and Neptune explain steps for building and installing it in different ways. Moreover, QtIVI only explains configuring it. Even if the user would just "qmake-make" it, it is not said, it should be installed with "make install"

Even though, it is might be clear for experienced developers where components are installed, it should be explained at least for key ones where they are. For example, Neptune only says "Run the following command in a terminal under the neptune3-ui installation directory", whereas "installation directory" is unknown. Not mentioning the fact that the command "./neptune3-ui " implies the the Neptune is started from the current directory. Plus the installation step is not mentioned before, which makes "installation directory" irrelevant.

summary: Document the implementation concept of the of the Companion App
description:
For former "Remote settings app" is now becoming "Companion App". Initially, the app was a part of the prototype to try our the use of Qt Remote Objects as a transport for APIs auto-generated from QFace. That prototype was very successful and fit well with many needs in Qt Auto. Among other aspects, the "Remote settings app" can serve as a reference implementation of a companion app which connects to the central ECU running the IVI and can access values via network which can be shown and changed on a remote device via network. Thanks Qt being cross-platform, and thanks a few design approaches in the existing "Remote settings app", this provides a complete app running the same way on any desktop or mobile device supporting Qt 5.12 and later.

A developer should understand the software architecture aspects applied to the implementation of the "Remote settings app". Reviewing of its code does not seem completely sufficient. This should be extended by a dedicated page in the docs as well as comments in the code itself if required.

summary: Testing of mvp on mac
description:
*Assumptions:*
 # Your mac has python 3.10 installed
 # You are using the bash shell on mach (e.g. iTerm)
 # Your ssh key has been uploaded to [https://git.qt.io|https://git.qt.io/]

*Steps to test:*

Setting up the environment
 # Clone QtCloud repo over ssh
 # Switch to *develop* branch and go to "dist" folder
 # Copy the qtci-0.0.1.zip to outside of the repository
 # Come back to where you copied the zip and unzip it there
 # Go to unzip folder and follow instructions given in README.txt

Or just follow these commands to setup the environment and do the testing:
{noformat}
$ git clone git@git.qt.io:playground/qtcloud.git qtcloud-ssh
$ cd qtcloud-ssh
$ git checkout -b develop -t origin/develop
$ cp dist/qtci-0.0.1.zip ../
$ cd ..
$ unzip qtcip-0.0.1.zip qtci-plugin-ssh
$ cd qtci-plugin-ssh
$ python3 01_install_venv.py
{noformat}
At this point, once the script has finished execution, it will give you a "next command" to configure the plugin. Copy the command as it is and replace:
 # /path/to/local/project with actual path of the repo you just cloned in step 1 (at qtcloud-ssh)
 # <gitlab_token> with your actual Gitlab token
 # <ngrok_token> with actual ngrok token

Execute this next command. Once the script finishes - it gives instructions on *how to run the plugin*. 

For example, if you are still in the *qtci-plugin-ssh* directory, then run the following script: *run-qtci.sh*. Once the script is running it will show an output like this: 

{noformat}
Hello world, Qt! (using python sys.version_info(major=3, minor=10, micro=1, releaselevel='final', serial=0))
 -> [ngrok] starting tunnel: OK. (url: https://64c7-87-95-116-39.ngrok.io)
 -> [gitlab] connecting to https://git.qt.io/playground/qtcloud: OK (project id: 1825)
 -> [gitlab] creating project webhook:  OK (url: https://64c7-87-95-116-39.ngrok.io/gitlab-incoming-3723)
 -> [httpd] starting local server at http://0.0.0.0:8086
{noformat}

At this point, open "http://localhost:8086" on your browser. It should shown something like this: 

 !screenshot-1.png|thumbnail! 

*If you have reached this point, everything is OK form installation of package perspective.*

summary: Improvement in our plugin usage - post installation
description:
Once the plugin has been installed, we should be able to create a new virtual environment for the plugin on demand. For example, as a developer, I have multiple projects where I want to use the Qt CI plugin, then I would like to have a utility which can create virtual environment for all such projects. 

*Alternative to this is that we install the virtual environment* at a place which the user does not tamper with. For example, on tighter integration with the Qt creator, this virtual environment could be created in Qt creator's plugin folder (or similar). Otherwise, this virtual environment could be created in *$USERHOME/virtual-env/qtci-venv*.  

Once the virtual environment has been created, we are going to install all the relevant dependencies including the "python pulgin for qtci". 

To create virtual environment and install dependencies: 

{code}
$ qtci-create-env /path/to/env 
{code}

We should have other utilities that:
# create config file
# run the ci plugin for project using the config file

The create config file should use "configparser" to store the following data:
# local project path
# gitlab where project is hosted (REST API)
# project path on gitlab
# gitlab private token
# ngrok token
# port where this project config will run
# anything else that makes sense

{code}
$ qtci-create-config -p local-project-path -g gitlab-token -n ngrok-token
{code}

For executing the plugin or CI plugin for that project:
{$code}
$ qtci-run-plugin -c /path/to/config/file
{$code}

All of these utilities: *qtci-create-env*, *qtci-create-config* and *qtci-run-plugin* should be added to the PATH after installation or at lease should be made available for the user to run from a folder they know about. 

Also, user should not be able to run *qtci-create-config* and *qtci-run-plugin* until a virtual environment has been created. _(On a side note, should we get rid of virtual environment for user?)_

Open discussions - until we have clarity on Qt creator integration:

# What is that one folder where we can store the plugin and its files?

After Qt creator integration: 

# Can we add some scripts to PATH from Qt creator directory?

*there is more to all of it that can come as a part of brainstorming*

Notes to self:
# use setuptools entrypoints for *qtci-create-env* script? and similar for others also?

summary: qtci_bin - create_config script should update the qtci settings
description:
At this moment, when the QtCi plugin is imported for the first time, a settings file is created in *USERHOME/QtCloud/settings.config*. As soon as the project config is created validated using *qtci-create-config*, the data is written in form of *.env* file in the __file__ path of *qtci-create-config*. 

In addition to this - we should also write the key-value pair to Qt cloud settings file. 

For example, we could save settings to a new section called *basename(local-project-path)*. 

{noformat}
[qtcloud]
GITLAB_URL = https://git.qt.io
GITLAB_TOKEN = <gitlab_token> 
...
{noformat}

summary: Utilities related to showing build info and summary in docker images
description:
We should have utilities in the docker images which provide 
 # Build info (like which build was used to produce this image)
 # Build summary (like which Qt version + CMAKE_PREFIX PATH and other relevant info)

 
{code:java}
$ qt-v6.2.3 -build-info
# shows the build info (of the CI job that created the docker image)

$ qt-v6.2.3 -summary
# shows summary of qt version, url of the repo, sha1 etc etc.

$ qt-v6.2.3 -howto
# shows how or what steps one should take to build the target application

  {code}
 

Same information should be made available for *qt-${qt-branch}_android, qt-${qt-branch}_wasm* and other such platforms. 

Such information helps us to track back any issues in the build and improve it accordingly.

summary: Improve CI pipeline for building docker images
description:
We should have the following stages: 
 * Build
 ** build qt5
 ** build qt6
 ** build qt6 + wasm (needs build qt6)
 * Test
 ** test qt5 (dependencies - build qt5)
 ** test qt6 (dependencies - build qt6)
 ** test qt6 + wasm (dependencies - build qt6)
 * Deploy
 ** docker push qt5 (dependencies - build qt5)
 ** docker push qt6 (dependencies - build qt6)
 ** docker push qt6+wasm (dependencies - build qt6+wasm)

 

This means that all the BUILD stages should have an artifact created (.tar.gz) which is passed to the relevant TEST and DEPLOY stages. In addition to this, a file should be created which contains relevant the name of the DOCKER_IMAGE, which can be used in the TEST, DEPLOY stages.

In the TEST and DEPLOY stages, we should use "docker load" to load from the tar.gz file and perform the relevant docker push. 

 

*Why this is important?* Because right now, we are building and pushing things already to DEPLOY, even when we have not tested the docker build. This will cause damage in long run.

summary: Improvements in our dockerfile for efficient build timings
description:
At this point of time, whenever we run a build, for example: Qt6, Qt6+WASM, then we spend at least 20 minutes each build (or GitLab job) in cloning and initializing the repository. 

 

This time can be reduced by using only ONE QT Clone that is reused for all builds. This also means that we have only ONE DOCKERFILE per platform. We can use the following layers: 

*Example of layers in qt.linux.dockerfile:*
 * Basic environment variable checks
 * Install build dependencies
 * Clone QT + Init repository + build Qt host (at: /opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-host)
 * If QT_WASM flag is set:
 ** Clone, initialize and activate Wasm SDK
 ** Make new build directory in QT_SRC for Qt-WASM-build
 ** Configure (--prefix=/opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-wasm -qt-host /opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-host)
 ** Build Qt for WASM with QtHost from previous step
 ** Install Qt to /opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-wasm
 * If QT_ANDROID flag is set
 ** Download relevant android SDK and build-tools
 ** Make new build directory in QT_SRC for Qt-Android-build
 ** Configure (--prefix=/opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-android/xxx -qt-host /opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-host)
 ** Build and install Qt for Android to /opt/qt/${QT_BRANCH}-android/xxx where xxx is the target (ABI) ({{armeabi-v7a;arm64-v8a;x86;x86_64)}}

 

At the end, we use this "ONE" single docker image to compile and test all applications and then, create separate docker images like: 
 # qt-${QT_BRANCH}_linux
 # qt-${QT_BRANCH}_wasm_linux
 # qt-$\{QT_BRANCH]_android_linux

*I am not sure that this ticket is required to be done immediately or not, but this definitely helps in saving time.* 

 

**Very soon, we will start to build for: 
 # Qt5
 # Qt6
 # Qt6+WASM
 # Qt6+Android+armeabi-v7a
 # Qt6+Android+arm64-v8a
 # Qt6+Android+x86
 # Qt6+Android+x86_64

*Advantages of this*:
 * With this process, we are possibly able to save at least 140 minutes spent in cloning Qt sources. 
 * We will have to maintain only one dockerfile for Qt+SDKs per platform as compared to different dockerfiles for all the above.
 * The same method can be repeated for supporting Qt docker images for MacOS and Windows.

description:
The idea is to be able to build docker image from any platform (linux, macos and windows). Right now, the docker-build wrapper is written in shell script and we should convert it to python script so that docker-* wrappers can be executed every where. 

Why do we have a wrapper for all of this? Because there are various --build-args that we pass on to the docker build command so that it is able to build the right image. With such wrapper written in python (and using the python docker sdk) we are able to simplify many things including the possibility of having 
 * one dockerfile for all platforms
 * comprehensive handling of building docker images for different platforms

This will also solve:

summary: Prepare docker image for Qt Android - armeabi-v7a
description:
Get inspiration from the code below: 

Preconditions: 
1. Use qt_v6.3.0_linux

2. Install Android SDK

3. Compile Qt for android - see below.

 
{code:java}
# Set ANDROID_ABI like this: ANDROID_ABI=armeabi-v7a;arm64-v8a;x86;x86_64
export IFS=";"
for abi in ${ANDROID_ABI}; do
    echo "Building Android for ABI ${abi}"
    cd ..
    mkdir qt-build-android-${abi} && cd qt-build-android-${abi}
    ../qt-src/configure -xplatform android-clang -android-abis ${abi} -qt-host-path ../qt-build-install -android-ndk /mnt/android-ndk/ -android-sdk /mnt/android-sdk -prefix ../qt-build-android-install-${abi}
    ninja
    cmake --install .
done
 {code}

summary: Create a start_env script for all docker images
description:
We should have a start_env script which takes care of exporting the right environment variables for the docker image. For example, the CMAKE_PREFIX or QT_HOST etc etc, so that the customer is able to just "export" that script and get to the environment where they can start to use the docker image. 

 

*Why this script is needed when we have ENV??*

One single usecase is that we install Java and for android, we need to export JAVA_HOME, In docker, we can't have one "layer" where we can find the path to JAVA_HOME and export it as ENV. This will be the case for all other similar variables. So, having a script will always make sure that the JAVA_HOME is calculated right and then is exported for the bash or shell terminal when user is using the cloud image.

summary: Onboarding: Setup a micro service which handles confidential stuff
description:
At this moment, we are running Qt ci plugin from user's computer and it's not safe to store secrets there. So, we should create a micro service and use this to retrieve credentials from the secret service.

We have to deliver: 
 * Python FastAPI implementation of following endpoints:
 ** <server>/api/has-qtcloud-licence
 *** params: Qt account email, Qt account password, plus some sha1 or hash for authentication to microservice?
 *** internally:
 **** Use discovery api
 **** Login and get JWT token
 **** Check if user has licence for Qt cloud
 **** Return TRUE or FALSE
 **** If TRUE, also return conan credentials
 ** <server>/api/get-git-admin-token
 *** params: some sha1 for authentication
 *** internally:
 **** return the git.qt.io's admin token
 ** (more end points to be checked)
 * Use a python3 alpine image in a dockerfile, copy this server there
 * Execute the server using Python FastAPI

IMportant: This MicroService should already contain the Login CODE for Qt account. So, we are going to send the Qt account + Password to this microservice and this uses the Qt account apis (discovery + login) etc to return relevant information for us to use in the Qt ci plugin code.

summary: Qt cloud dashboard configuration
description:
Related to #2.

The developer should have a wizard which they can use to configure the Qt cloud inside their Qt creator. At this moment, Qt cloud configuration is local to every project, however at some point, it should make sense to associate it with the Qt cloud account.

Based on the current code base of this MVP repository (commit 4f34519) the Qt cloud dashboard needs at least the following:
 * Gitlab URL `e.g. [https://git.qt.io|https://git.qt.io/]`
 * User's private token `e.g. your_Private_token`
 * Project path `e.g. playground/qtcloud`

In order to also manage the local git repository, we would also need the path of the Git repo which is being managed by this dashboard.

 
 * Other important things:
 ** If the user is cloning repo using our utility, then we are storing the "CLONED_PATH_LOCAL"
 ** However, if the user has already cloned the repo, then we should auto detect the:
 *** <auto detect> Gitlab URL
 *** <auto detect> Project path
 *** <ask user> Gitlab private token

summary: Simplify the CI pipeline for docker images repo
description:
Right now, all builds related to docker are executed in docker-images repository. We should break this in form of a "Gitlab project chain". So, this is how the builds should happen:
 # SRC repo - hello-world-qtcloud
 # Qt6Base repo - Qt6 docker image
 ## Qt6Base+WASM
 ## Qt6Base+Android_x86
 ## Qt6Base+Android_x86_64
 ## Qt6Base+Android_arm7
 ## Qt6Base+Android_arm8
 ## Qt6Base+Yocto
 # Qt5Base repo - Qt5 docker image
 ## Qt6Base+Android

All of these projects should have the SRC repo as a git-submodule and have separate .gitlab-ci.yml which triggers relevant QtDockerBuild based on the configuration. 

 

As a proof of concept, it is OK to do this with python scripts (and not docker images) where SRC creates python module "HelloWorld", which is imported in QtBase as "HelloWorldQt" and in Wasm and Android images as "HelloWorldQt+Wasm", "HelloWorldQt+Android".

summary: Update Emscripten version in Qt+WASM Docker containers
description:
The version of Emscripten SDK used in WebAssembly docker containers should be updated to be compatible with the Qt version used inside the container. [https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/wasm.html] states some minimum version that we probably should follow.

At least with Qt6.3.1 + WASM container the old version leads to some problems
 * `emrun` doesn't work inside the container
 * build errors might occur

To be confirmed, if similiar problems exist with Qt6.3.0 and older versions

root cause is the mapping `emsdk_version = "3.0.0" if branch == qt_branch_630 else "2.0.14"` in the image creation.

summary: Study how Boot2Qt currently works, and how to run the build process in CI
description:
In order to get Yocto support to QT Cloud, we need to be able to produce Boot2Qt compatible binaries in CI. In this phase, we need to restrict the support for only Boot2Qt -distribution and the supported embedded platforms need to be defined.

As an initial PoC:
 * Study, how the build process for Boot2Qt currently works in Qt Creator. Create a simple example project, build, and deploy it to actual embedded HW
 * Check the existing work on containerizing the toolchain, and check if the Dockerfiles from there can be used in CI, as-is or with some modifications
 * Build the example project from step 1 in CI, and verify that the end result works on actual embedded HW.

summary: Build Qt from a patch

Naming convention of the build: *qt_v<base_version>_<patch_name_or_purpose>_<platform>*

We shall apply the patch using `patch -p0`

 

Few other concerns that we have at this moment:
 * Should we run Qt unit tests after patch is applied?
 * How should we determine the quality of the Qt after patch?
 * Anything else?

summary: Image build pipeline should accept any tag/branch inside minor Qt versions
description:
At moment, the `qt_docker.py` tool in `docker-images` repo accepts only certain, hardcoded branches to build qt. It should be modified to accept any tag, at least bugfix releases inside minor releases. For example, it should be allowed to build all `6.4.z` -versions without changes to that file whenever a new bugfix release is released by Qt.

There are some per-branch dependencies for external tools like emscripten and Android SDKs, but they usually change only between Qt minor versions, not between bugfix releases. Therefore these checks should be happen at the level of minor version.

summary: QT_WASM_CMAKE_PATH does not have --build as an argument
description:
When we provide the toolchain path in qt-cmake script, the build argument does not work.                                     
                                       
  • docker-container # source /opt/qt_wasm.env
    •                                    
  • docker-container # source $$EMSCRIPTEN_SDK_ENV_FILE
    •                                    
  • docker-container [Qt+WASM 6.3.1]# cd /path/to/your/source/code/dir1
    •                                    
  • docker-container [Qt+WASM 6.3.1]# $QT_WASM_CMAKE_PATH CMakeLists.txt
    •                                    
  • docker-container [Qt+WASM 6.3.1]# $QT_WASM_CMAKE_PATH --build . --verbose
    •                                
Ultimately. qt-cmake does not allow --build

summary: Use setup.py to package Qt CI
description:
Benefits of using setup.py
 # Creates a package which other users can install using PIP
 # Qt creator can also install the package using PIP
 # Or Qt creator can ship with this PIP and install it in the VENV created during installation
 # Easy to maintain. To update the list of new features, we do not really need the code change, just update the "manifest.in" file
 # This is how all standard python modules are shipped
 # Easy scaleable to multiple projects

Plus a lot of stuff which can be managed better as compared to one single script.

Ultimately, when setup.py is implemented we can do something like:
 # python setup.py bdist <-- to build
 # Deliver the content of dist/qtci-version.tar.gz to Qt creator team for integration
 # Qt creator can install this plugin using pip install qtci-version.tar.gz

------------------------------------

*Update / Jan 21, 2022*

In order to achieve this, there would be small changes that are needed in our repository structure. For example, have the *src* directory structure renamed to something like this: 

 
{noformat}
src/
    bin/
    CHANGES.txt
    docs/
    LICENSE.txt
    MANIFEST.in
    README.txt
    setup.py
    qtci/
          __init__.py
          run.py
          sub_modules/
              __init__.py
              ngrok.py
              gitlab.py
              gitpython.py
              server.py 
{noformat}

IN addition to this, we have our static assets - like html pages, javascript libraries etc - that should be packaged as well.

summary: Investigate how to document the global functions available with a module
description:
Qt Core offers convenience headers such as, <QtMath>, <QtAlgorithm>, and so on, which offer a few functions. Some of the functionality offered by these headers are available with the module import in Python. For example, qAcos(), qAtan(), qAsin(), and many more.

In Qt, such functionality is documented using qdoc's \headerfile command. But in Python, we don't need to include any additional  imports to access the functions. We should investigate how we can include the existing documentation for these functions in the Qt for Python documentation.

description:
Implementing editor inside QML Puppet process is in fact something not done yet (in 2D), so that actually needs further study and prototyping to see how that will work.

Challenges lie in how to synch the data model on Qt Creator side so that the user doesn’t see after dropping the object it jumping to it’s previous position and then back to where he dropped it.

summary: Timeline key findings
description:
This task states the result of my research of the timeline.

The timeline works consistently for 2D and 3D properties so nothing needs to be implemented for handling 3D properties.

Below are my findings after trying the timeline for a while. Those items vary from bugs to UX issues. Some items need discussion with the UX specialist. Also some items are a quick fix, some require some effort. They are not in any specific order:
* Playhead snapping is missing.
* Keyframe icon should be smaller.
* Clicking and dragging the ruler should move the playhead not start the selection rect.
* Why do I have to add/remove timelines? IMO there should always exist 1 timeline.
* When changing the timeline's start/end keyframe(s), make sure the playhead stays within the new range.
* Selection rect should select a keyframe based on center point not the whole keyframe rect.
* Playhead vertical line should cover the full height of the timeline view.
* When dragging a keyframe the clicked point within the keyframe should be preserved so that the keyframe doesn't do a sudden jump upon starting the dragging.
* Status bar should be specific about whether the Frame # is a selected keyframe or the playhead frame.
* Status bar should update when moving a keyframe.
* Context menu action "Edit Value for keyframe..." Shoud be "Edit Keyframe..." and allows editing both keyframe's time and value so that it is possible to accurately set a keyframe's time.
* Although you cannot move a keyframe beyond the timeline's limits, you can move the keyframe's animation beyond limits which will move the starting/ending keyframe beyond the timeline limits.
* If you drag the playhead beyond the timeline's limits, the playhead either jumps to an animation range keyframe or disappears upon mouse release.
* A property on the timeline is animated in the range between the timeline start and the first keyframe. The part before the first keyframe should have the same value as the first keyframe.
* When removing a timeline the status bar should be emptied.

summary: Create 3D Edit View technical proof-of-concept
description:
*What is needed*

Create rough cut technical feasibility proof-of-concept to support architecture planning of visual 3D editing inside Qt Design Studio.

*Who needs this*

This is needed by the Qt Creator/Qt Design Studio developers to iron out basic technical issues from the system (consisting of Qt Creator, Qt Quick 3D, QML, Qt Design Studio) before we start more detailed feature development.

*Why it's needed*

Adding support for 3D editing brings new requirements above and beyond the 2D edit features in Qt Design Studio. We've already proven some of these features can cause issues, will require refactoring Qt Creator code etc. It is critical to first get a rough technical proof of concept done that irons out these basic problems and proves the 3D editor features can be implemented. After this we can then move to finalize all the features to meet the exact UX designs etc.

*Acceptance criteria*

All depicted sub-tasks can be proven to work. The UX might be really rough at this point, but the feature works and can be used in the edit view PoC.

summary: Add prefix and generate id's from layer options
description:
In discussions with customers it was brought up that we could have a couple of quality of life features added to the photoshop bridge (and presumably if it makes sense to all bridges)
 # Generate all id's from the layer name - At the moment it is a lot of work to name all the layers and then manually enter all the qml id's - most people seem to want them to be the same in the end. We should add an advanced feature that allows users to generate the id's from the layer name. (with the understanding that they must be unique and qml friendly layer names)
 # Have a field where a project prefix can be added to every qml id automatically. Some projects follow a specific naming convention where every file must be prefixed with the project id. We could have 1 field for this and save the users a lot of time copy / pasting.

 

Implementation details (Requirements):
 * Add QML id prefix & suffix settings in settings page
 * Serialize these strings in the document metadata.
 * The prefix and suffix strings shall be added to auto-generated QML ids by default
 * The prefix and suffix shall not apply if the user explicitly updates the QML id.
 * Add a button here "Reset", clicking the reset button will reapply the suffix & prefix to all qml ids. Show a warning before doing this.

summary: The way we load fonts with Loaders is not reliable
description:
The way we load fonts with Loaders is not reliable

We use a FontLoader to load all fonts in the 'fonts' folder.
This is not reliable, because fonts are loaded after text items are shown.
Therefore the font is not used. 
This issue is 'hidden' when using the live preview because the document is loaded multiple times.

*Who Needs This*
All users who edit 3D scenes in Qt Design Studio

*Why It's Needed*
This user story will take the technical proof-of-concept level implementation of 3D view navigation and helper gizmos to level that follows UX design and is approved by UX.

*Acceptance Criteria*
3D edit view navigation is implemented in a way that is approved by UX design.

summary: We have to redesign how effects work in QDS
description:
*We have to redesign how effects work in QDS*

Effects as different items to not work very well. 
We should consider using Item: layer.effect instead.

Issues

* Stacking of effects is not directly possible and requires stacking items
* The effects are a component and properties cannot be exposed as alias properties
* How will effects with two source items work (e.g. Blend/OpacityMask)?

Most likely effects that 'combine/blend' two items like Blend and OpacityMask will continue to inherit Item and therefore be a separate Item. As a result, the setup of such an effect will stay more complicated than in other tools.

*Ideally, blend effects would be part of Item, the scenegraph. Any item could be blended against the background or use the background as an opacity mask.*
This would mean no extra items/setup is required to blend/mask an item and the usability would be similar to other tools.
Is this feasible for Qt 6?

summary: Highlight selected icon on the toolbar
description:
Currently it is really difficult to see which tool is selected in 3D edit view (item/ group selection, rotation, scale etc).The colour of panes and toolbars is dark, so adding black background for selected tool is difficult to notice. In addition, icons are black & white, plus small icon size and makes it difficult to notice if icon appearance changes.

So it should be easier to see immediately the tool states. Basically it means we need to change current theme: 
- Coloring an icon when it is selected (also hover state needs better indication), 
-  different background color 
- or adding a border color. 

Current selection color (blue) would be suitable. Another option to add contrast for selection is to change the color of the UI to less dark.

However, colour changes should be done in a consistent way, not only to 3D Edit View. How to proceed needs to be agreed and also take into account does these changes affect to Qt Creator.

summary: Improving Light gizmos and icons
description:
Below are some items I have in mind to improve the look of the light icons and gizmos. Please check them and validate, improve or reject them.
 * Directional light geometry should have fixed size irrespective of the camera zoom as it doesn't really have a size.
 * Directional light direction lines length match the light intensity?
 * Selected light's gizmo should be yellow.
 * Light gizmo should appear only when the light is selected, otherwise only the icon appears.
 * If the point above is rejected, at least the disabled gizmo color be black or very dark gray (currently it is barely distinguishable from the background).
 * Area light gizmo lines should be semi-randomly distributed over the light area or at least add a fifth line at the center.
 * Area light size should not be fixed. Should match light width and height.
 * Area light direction lines length match the light intensity?
 * point light gizmo should be a sphere matching the effective volume of the light.
 * Spot light gizmo diameter and height should match the light properties.
 * "Scale" property should be disabled for lights? I cannot see the meaning of scaling a light.
 * IMO Light icons should be improved (check attached unity light icons as an example). Of course we also need to fix the issue that causes icons to have the weird gradient they have currently.

 * Make 3D Editor onboarding text translatable (QDS-1993).
 * Delay item library update if content can't be resolved (QDS-2023).
 * Fix navigator doesn't expand nor show selection of a DnD'ed 3D object when navigator is collapsed and no selection (QDS-2024).

There are quite a lot text that is directed to  developer and that makes you think who is the  target user, especially in the beginning of the documentation.  Would it be possible to have section for Designer and Developers? 

Now, for example User interface section should mention which parts are important for Design studio user (designer) and also mention that parts 2-5 are for developing purposes and designer does not necessary have to work with kits, debug or classes and functions. 

Other examples: 
“Qt Design Studio caters not only to developers who are used to using the mouse, but also to developers who are more comfortable with the keyboard. A wide range of keyboard and navigation shortcuts are available to help speed up the process of developing your application.”

“If you receive a freely scalable icon in the SVG format from an UI designer, you can export it to several images of different sizes to create a set of pixmaps. You can then use QIcon::addPixmap() to add the pixmaps to icons in different modes and states.”
	
There are also some old images, for example in layouts.

summary: UI support for TextureInput properties
description:
Some Quick3D effects and many custom materials have their textures wrapped in TextureInput properties. Changing those textures need to be enabled in UI similarly to Texture properties. These textures typically have a default value, which should be possible to restore after texture has been changed. 

Fixing this probably requires changing the effect/custom material definitions so that the default texture is not defined inline in TextureInput.texture property.

summary: Handle Virtual parent export type.
description:
A "Virtual" export type is created in the metadata to have similar DOM when importing-exporting between QML and PSD.

AssetImported plugin has to handle this virtual group layer.

 

Changes:
 * Make such layers as locked so that it can't be deleted accidentally. (Update: Locking is not a good idea. This disables the edit also)
 * Handle Virtual export type in Qt-Bridge.
 ** The export type of virtual parent layers should be disabled.
 ** The immediate child can not be set as merged.
 * Add child layers of virtual parent layers to their appropriate parent while exporting metadata in Qt-Bridge

There should be some way to allow executing a custom step when an item is dragged from item library into the project.

For example, when dragging a Quick3D CustomMaterial to project, it would be nice to also copy or generate a basic shader files, so that the material is immediately useful. 

There are other potential uses beyond simply copying extra files, such as launching a customization wizard for the item.

Ideally this would be a new block in the ItemLibraryEntry that specifies a factory and arguments.

summary: Integrate Crashpad with Qt Creator and Qt Design Studio
description:
It is required to add Google's Crashpad ([https://chromium.googlesource.com/crashpad/crashpad]) to Qt Design Studio to reports crashes to our backend (sentry.io is chosen).

Crashpad starts a process (crash_handler) that handles crashes in the assigned process (Qt Design Studio in this case).

When a crash happens:
 * Crashpad's running crash_handler process captures a snapshot of the crashed process and save it to minidump file (.dmp).
 * The .dmp file is uploaded to our backend.
 * A record in added to the backend with the crash details (call stack, OS, architecture, etc)

For the call stack to appear correctly on the backend, debug information files (DIF) needs to be uploaded to sentry backend as well. Uploading debug symbols happens using the tool (sentry-cli) provided by sentry.io. We need to upload as much diffs as possible that are used to build Design Studio in order for the call stack to appear as complete as possible.

To reduce the size of debug information symbols another tool (dump_syms) - provided by Crashpad - converts DIFs to .sym format which has significantly less file size.

More about how Crashpad works here:
 [https://chromium.googlesource.com/crashpad/crashpad/+/HEAD/doc/overview_design.md|https://chromium.googlesource.com/crashpad/crashpad/+/HEAD/doc/overview_design.md#Snapshot]

Crashpad relies on chromium depot_tools for building. The full details of how to build crashpad are here:
 [https://chromium.googlesource.com/crashpad/crashpad/+/HEAD/doc/developing.md]

summary: Read MCU metadata from QML file
description:
We accumulated quite a few meta data for MCU support.

This should be parsed from a QML file using QmlJS::SimpleReader.

The location of the file should be Core::ICore::resourcePath() + "qmldesigenr/qt4mcu"

The hardcoded values and lists can then be replaced by data from this files.

This can be implemented using a singleton. The singleton should also contain the isMcu function so it is not spread out over the codebase.

The singleton should have a refresh function taking a version.
Depending on the version it could load a different configuration.
In the first iteration, the version is ignored.

summary: Clarify Sketch plugin installation
description:
Clarify Sketch plugin installation

There was some confusion about: https://doc.qt.io/qtdesignstudio/qtbridge-sketch-setup.html#:~:text=You%20can%20use%20the%20installation,available%20at%20Plugins%20%3E%20Qt%20Bridge.

The plugin is not an executable, but it is installed by double clicking (qt-bridge.sketchplugin ).
This means the plugin is associated with Sketch and can be installed by double clicking, but is no executable.

Qt Bridge for Sketch is delivered as a Sketch plugin package.

To set up Qt Bridge for Sketch:

1. Double-click qt-bridge.sketchplugin in the sketch_bridge folder in the
   installation directory of Qt Design Studio.
2. Sketch will automatically install the Sketch Bridge
3. You can launch the Sketch plugin from the Plugins file menu in Sketch.

summary: Describe the properties of most commonly-used QML types
description:
The current approach for the 2D types is to link to the QML or Qt Quick module documentation. Because the property names and their location in the UI don't altogether match those in the modules, this can be confusing and requires an extra effort from the reader.

Therefore, describe using the following often needed types in more detail:
 * Shapes
 * Text
 * Images
 * User interaction methods
 * Lists and other data models
 * Animation types
 * Visual Effects

Also move information about "Positioning Items" to a separate topic and describe the properties of the Positioner and Layout types in more detail.

This approach is already used for 3D types: [https://doc.qt.io/qtdesignstudio/studio-3d-components.html]

description:

This has implications on performance and is not required.

Early versions had only a few views that were usually all visible.
This has changed, and it should be possible to "disable" the callbacks.

summary: improve rotation in 2d
description:
Introduce a discrete rotation tool for rotating 2d objects in the form editor.

Currently rotation can only be achieved by using the property in the advanced tab. Items will rotate around the origin point selected in the advanced properties. Both of these properties should be moved to the item geometry section.

We want to introduce a toggle tool in the form editor menu that when active allows you to drag on an item to rotate it.

Dragging should move the rotation in it's smallest step size, dragging while holding shift should lock the drag to 5° steps.

Currently after an item has been rotated it is no longer possible to interact with the transform corners of the item, it would be great if that can be fixed as well.

summary: Add the ability to update objects within a scene
description:
When importing a scene into design studio it creates a new component that includes this scene. Modifications of that scene like material setup and eventually lighting are then done inside this component.

If the user realises too late that something is missing from this scene or that some objects need to be refined there is currently no way to simply replace the outdated version of that objects with the new version without changing the scene-graph (importing would result in another component and not just that one object) or throwing away all the work already done. 

It would be nice to have an "update object" feature that simply swaps the old version with the new one.

summary: Add mini trace to Qt Creator/QDS
description:
Add minitrace library to Qt Creator (https://github.com/hrydgard/minitrace).

The library hs to be added as third party library and we should add a simple C++ API on top. 
Release builds should be able to generate traces. 
We most likely need two trace levels (*only profile builds* and *all builds*)

Adding tracepoints and evaluating them graphically is a great help for profiling since we do not have to rely on debug symbols and the manual tracepoints create less noise.
Every view/widget can add tracepoints during initiation, which makes it easy to track "slow" views. Similarly, we can trace the different parts/steps of the QML model.
Eventually, this might allow regression tests for performance.

summary: Update the merge algorithm to be more predictable.
description:
The proposed changes will make the imported QML the source of truth for the DOM.
 * Any node inserted under a node imported from Asset Importer will maintain its position in the DOM
 * All properties shall be synched from the old node to the new node
 * In case of property clash, the source of truth is the new QML unless it's a Binding property.
 * Heuristics shall be used to match the node, especially when the UUIDs are missing.

summary: Using the list for flow tags to priotize imports in the "import list/combo box"
description:
I noticed that you removed the "FlowTags" and this was probably the right decision. 

The FlowTags was just a "hack" to make the crucial imports more discoverable. 

I suggest using the list for the FlowTags to prioritize imports in the list when adding modules.

for example, the modules that formerly had a FlowTag could be on top, or we add a quick filter that only shows modules that had a FlowTag.

Currently, the list is very long and the user has to use the search to find modules. Also, it is not clear which modules are useful. My guess is that in 90% of the cases users want to add a module from the "FlowTags" list. So having those modules on the top should make things a lot easier.

summary: Create an example or a tutorial for View3D resizing while keeping visual size constant
description:
Create either an example or a tutorial with Qt Design Studio that showcases (at least) the dynamic layer resize ([https://doc-snapshots.qt.io/qt3dstudio/layers.html#dynamic-resize]) feature parity issue with Qt 3D Studio ([https://intranet.qt.io/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=93455952]).

The QDS project should have at least two View3Ds:
 * One of them, the background "layer" can remain the same size the whole time
 ** If this View3D doesn't have animated things, it can use Progressive AA
 * The other one should have something that first fills the screen, but when rotated, fills only a small part of the screen (for example a rocket)
 ** The View3D in this one should be resized so that it only uses as much space on the screen as it really needs
 *** this requires adjusting camera properties together with the resizing, so that the visual size remains the same (i.e. the rocket is the same size it would be if the View3D wasn't resized)
 ** This resized View3D should then have the maximum SSAA turned on

* *NEW* Open generated .qrc file (_temp_)

* *NEW* Show all files (_<file></file>_) in QTableWidget (see e.g. addimagesdialog.cpp)
* *NEW* Each file has a checkbox
* *NEW* Unchecked files are removed from the XML file/dom
* *NEW* Save changed .qrc file

summary: Split Resource Generation into two Action
description:
*Split Resource Generation into two Action*

Currently, there exists only one action that generates a .qmlrc file which is actually a .rcc file

auto action = new QAction(QCoreApplication::translate("QmlDesigner::GenerateResource", "Generate Resource File"));

This action should be split into two actions.

ne action would be called* "Generate QRC Resource File"* and 'should just' generate the .qrc file.
The second action called
*"Generate RCC Resource File"* should generate the .rcc file like the current action.

When generating the .rcc file the file dialog should give the opinion of .qmlrc or .rcc with .qmlrc as the default.

You can use Project::AllFiles

auto currentProject = ProjectExplorer::SessionManager::startupProject();
currentProject->files(Project::AllFiles);

This should return all files from the project.

By default, only files from the project should be checked.

Certain files can be always hidden in the table and can be always ignored:
*.qmlproject, .pro, .pri, .qtds. user *

So instead of checking all files by default, only 'project files' should be checked in the table.

summary: QRC file integration
description:
Qt-based C++ project typically use .qrc files to manage resources like .qml files.

QDS should it make easy to keep .qrc files in sync with the .qmlproject files.

QDS should create new .qrc files from scratch but also update existing .qrc files with the files defined in the .qmlproject. 

When generating a .qrc file an existing .qrc file can be chosen and QDS will add the files from the .qmlproject to the .qrc file. The user can uncheck/remove files from the .qrc file or add files in the project folder but not part of the .qmlproject. 

It is a use case to remove files already add to the .qrc file because they are in the .qrc file but not in the .qmlproject. Files in the .qmlproject should be bold in the UI, to make it easy to identify files not in the .qmlproject and only in the .qrc file.

C++ projects will already have a .qrc file created by their wizard.

summary: Create a few particle system presets
description:
A few good particle system presets should be available in item library. A couple of really simple ones and a couple of little more complex ones. Implementation could be similar to how different models (Cube, Sphere, etc.) are done, i.e. by providing a short source template for each type. In component library we should probably have separate category "QtQuick3D Premade Particle Systems" or something along those lines, which contains these.

These should be designed by a technical artist, as they would know best what kind of preset particle systems make sense.

summary: Create cpp application for Coffee Machine example using the new cmake API
description:
With Qt 6.2 comes a new cmake API how to integrate .qml files into a C++ project.



We have an existing example project using .qrc files (https://git.qt.io/public-demos/qtdesign-studio/-/tree/master/playground/cppdemoproject)
this demo project contains two .qrc files. One for the actual project and one for the QDS dependencies.

The goal is to take our Coffee Machine example and turn it into a cmake project with a main.cpp using the new QML API.

https://github.com/qt/qtdeclarative/blob/dev/tests/auto/qml/qmlbasicapp/CMakeLists.txt
https://github.com/qt/qtdeclarative/blob/dev/tests/auto/qml/qmlbasicapp/BasicExtension/CMakeLists.txt

qt6_add_qml_module

The idea is to have a main CMakeLists.txt for the cpp parts that includes another CMakeLists.txt from a qml sub folder that defines the .qml parts.
We could have a third CMakeLists.txt for the QDS modules (Studio Controls).

You can add a subfolder with a new  CMakeLists.txt: *add_subdirectory()*

summary: Create icons for toggling the particle view in puppet
description:
Create icons for toggling the particle view on or off in 3D View.

The normal icon 1x size is 16x16 pixels and the 2x size (which gets used on 4k displays) is 32x32 pixels. Bit depth is 8 and they are grayscale masks. The background dark and light color comes from the code.

4 icons are needed in total
 * 16x16 for 'off' state (particles_off.png)

 * 32x32 for 'off' state (particles_off@2x.png)

 * 16x16 for 'on' state (particles_on.png)

 * 32x32 for 'on' state (particles_on@2x.png)

The icon is placed on the top right corner next to the refresh button,  and is togglable (see particles_icon_puppet.png).

 'On' state has darker background (see particles_icon_on.png)

 'Off' state background is the color of the menu bar (see particles_icon_off.png)

The function of this toggle button is to enable or disable particle animations in the 3D editor.

summary: [Research] Variant support
description:
Research how to implement proper variant support to be able to create vanilla release and change customization just by switching the variant.

Areas to study:
* Support State Syntax
* Detect if a State Variant is found in the Variant name syntax
* If a State Variant is found keep track of id’s in each Variant
* If id’s match keep track of property changes 
* Create States in qds and apply property changes to the correct State
* If a merge template is known (Button) and a state is know (Hover) add the correct when condition

* Detect if Theme Variant is found in the Variant name syntax
* If Theme Variant is found and Colours use the Style name, keep track of which theme is applied
* Apply the correct id in each case, or apply the appended id generated in creating the library style

* Detect if another non-qml Variant is defined (Brand)
* Keep track of id’s and property changes between id’s
* Either a) creates states with Variants full syntax
(Brand=QDS > brand-qds and Brand=Creator > brand-creator)
Or b) Create Components with variants value appended.

description:
*Use AuroraCluster example as template for wizards and cmakfiles.txt generation*

See: https://git.qt.io/public-demos/qtdesign-studio/-/tree/master/playground/AuroraCluster

All generated files that are supposed to be regenerated now contain a comment.
main.cpp and the main cmakefiles.tst do not contain this commen, since we expect users to change those.

The parts from main.cpp and the main cmakefiles.txt that are expected to change again are 
included from external files (qmlmodules and import_qml_plugins.h)

qmlmodules contains the QML specfic parts and links each module. If modules are added this file would change. The same applies to import_qml_plugins.h. The header file ensures that the linked does not discard the modules, since for each module now a symbol is directly referenced.

The files main.cpp and  import_qml_plugins.h were moved to a "src" folder and the main QML module is always called 'content'.

To avoid name clashes the main applicatin target is called ProjectNameApp, so it does not clash with the module of the same name.

Each cmakefiles.txt for QML contains a statement like this: qt_add_library(Data STATIC)
This statement ensures that the module is statically linked which makes deployment easier, but requires_ import_qml_plugins.h_ and the explicit linkage in _qmlmodules_.

* Treeview or node based
* Shows connections between pages and tracked components

summary: Image cache support project thumbnail
description:
We need a thumbnail for recent projects.

Each project created by the latest wizard has a component call App.qml (content/App.qml).

We already generate a thumbnail for this component.
 !image-2021-12-20-13-55-35-455.png|thumbnail! 

Whenever a project is opened an App.qml does exist we want to store the thumbnail in a seperate image cache. The key should be the project name.

In the welcome page we can check if the thumbnail exists (using the project name) and retrieve the thumbnail for the recent projects.

The thumbnail image cache can be used by a specific image provider in the welcome page.
The Studio Welcome Page already has a dependency on the QmlDesigner.

summary: Thumbnails for projects need to be updated
description:
Thumbnails for projects need to be updated.

When the project is initially opened we generate a thumbnail. 
 But we do not automatically regenerate a thumbnail when the project is changed.

App.qml is usually not changed updated, but other files that influence how App.qml is looking do change.

When a new project is generated the thumbnail is usually a gray rectangle. 

Regenerating the thumbnail on close has issues, but we could remove outdated previews from the cache so that they get regenerated.

summary: Add timing logic for closing modal
description:
When opening the pop ups for the vents or seat settings, we should give a chance to the user to let it close on its own without having to press the close button.

For this reason, we can give a time limit for the pop-up to close on its own.

It should be based on inactivity by users: when the user is not touching the screen for a X time, the pop-up will close on its own.

The time should be around 10 seconds, but we need to verify to see what feels more natural.

summary: Integrate download an extraction and keep examples after download
description:
Currently, the examples are download each time over and over.

Instead:

1) Download the examples once to QStandardPaths::Documents + '/QtDesignStudio'+ version.
    This path should be the default but configurable in settings.
2) The download icon only appears if the example is already downloaded
3) When the example is opened and the first time it is also downloaded
  -- download and extration happens automatically. Afterwards the example is opened.
  -- To keep track of extraction progress we need the hardcoded number of files in the 
      ExampleModel
4) If an example is downloaded it can be redownloaded by clicking on the download/cloud icon.


The progress bar should have two stages. Download and Extraction. This requires a label.

summary: Research Spike: Get Qt 6.2/6.3 based Qt for Webassembly build of design viewer working
description:
There exists already a web viewer for .qmlrc files:

https://www.qt.io/blog/web-based-qt-design-viewer
https://qt-webassembly.io/designviewer/

qmake
make install

We should follow what Qt does for e.g. Qt Quick Controls 2.

qtquick3d\src\effects is the simplest example I found.
(https://github.com/qt/qtquick3d/tree/dev/src/effects)

summary: Use Qt6 shadertools from within Qt Design Studio
description:
When vertex and fragment shader files are edited, Qt Design Studio picks the change and tries to apply them to Shadereffect - BUT it does not work in Qt6 as Qt6 uses binary shader format.

Existing toolchain needs to be changed so, that when Qt Design Studio sees frag or vert shader saved, it needs to trigger 'qbs' binary and compile the shaders.

Resulting artifact is stored in the same directory where shader source was.

If there are errors, 'qsb' tool directs to stderr so they can be shown in Qt Design Studio's output pane.

summary: Get basic behaviour of landing page right
description:
The landing page is shown if QmlDesigner is disabled and the user opens .ui.qml file.

The landing page informs about Qt Design Studio and shows various options. (See https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QDS-6563)

The landing page contains a checkbox *(a)*: 
Always Open with Qt Design Studio. (Whenever a .ui.qml file is opened we launch QDS instead. This requires a .qmlproject file that will also be opened)
This option is disabled by default. If enabled The landing page is not opened anymore. 

Even if the automatic switch to design mode is disabled by the checkbox *(a),* the user can show the landing page by choosing the design mode for a .ui.qml file. The option is already implemented in qmlproject plugin using the notification bars.

The landing page has to check if QDS is installed. The check is already implemented in the qmlproject plugin.
If QDS is not installed the checkbox *(a)* can not be enabled.
Instead, a link is displayed (https://www.qt.io/design). This can later be refined to open the maintance tool.

If QDS is installed the landing page contains two buttons. One will open the ui.qml file in QDS the other will switch back to the edit mode.


This functionality should be sufficient to replace the info bars.

summary: Reduce hardcoded delay after 3D import
description:
There is 2 second hardcoded delay after 3D import puppet exists after the import. According to code comment this is done to allow little time for file operations to finish. IIRC if there is no extra delay, import will sometimes fail on creator side as not all files can be seen yet.

It should be possible to reduce this delay while still keeping operations reliable. Maybe QFileSystemWatcher can be utilized to check when it's safe to exit puppet process?

summary: Imported Quick3D components without a root node id dont render in 3D View

 * import a 3D model.
 * Create a 3D Scene and add the imported model to it.
 * Go inside the imported model (F2).
 * If the root node doesn't have an id, it doesn't render in the 3D View.
 * If you assign the root node an id, it appears in the 3D View.

Expected result:
model should render in the 3D View even if its root node doesn't have an id.

summary: Remove timestamp in bridge metadata name
description:
Bridge metadata file creates a new file with timestamp on Bridge export.  On import it creates a folder for with that name.  If I want to change the design and merge the QML, I have to make sure I'm saving over the previous metadata file, which isn't default (except for in the Sketch bridge).  

So by default in Figma, every time I export, it creates a new metadata file with a timestamp in the name.  Importing this into design studio creates a new import folder regardless of "merge qml" because of the unique file name in the metadata file. 

 

I propose not having a timestamp in the metadata file name/ or make it an optional suffix to add.

summary: Allow "infinite vector" zoom in the form editor
description:
Allow "infinite vector" zoom in the form editor.

Currently, we render all items at the original resolution and zoom in on the pixels.
We could offer a mode in which we increase the resolution while zooming in.

For document-level SVG and text items, this would be easy. But typically the document contains
sub-components that would have to be rendered at a higher resolution because we do not know how they work internally.
Rendering items at higher resolution might take a lot of memory.

We could implement this in a naive way up to a zoom level of 4x which might be sufficient for most use cases.

Zooming in would not be wysiwyg anymore.

summary: Use sensible defaults instead of validation checks
description:
In the model there can be invalid states. Mostly because of the removal of elements. Originally my idea was that strong checks would force people to fix their ownership. So if a node is removed all owned model nodes would be checked. But because it is much easier to fix a crash(caused by the exceptions) at the point of the crash a simple isValid() check is used. This is leading to much code clutter. Over time people copied that approach as a new pattern and tested everywhere for invalid nodes. Even for invalid root notes which should not be possible.

So my proposal is to remove the checks in the functions and simple return sensible defaults. So for an invalid node no parents, properties are returned etc..

summary: Add OpenSSL (v1) in Qt Design Studio packages
description:
Qt Design Studio requires OpenSSL for e.g. downloading examples (https). Qt 6.3 binaries support only OpenSSL v1 and Qt installer only provides OpenSSL v1.

Many of the recent Linux distributions support only OpenSSL v3 with their default repositories. Therefore Qt Design Studio packages should come with OpenSSL v1 at least until Qt supports OpenSSL v3 and that's also available in the installer as prebuilt binary for macOS and Windows.

This ticket is about making sure that the export clarification is up to date for Qt Design Studio and also for adding the OpenSSL (v1) in Qt Design Studio packages.

summary: Create QML components only when the metadata source is different than the one used to create it.
description:
The initial idea to achieve this:
 # create a hash from the (normalized) JSON data of each QML component.
 # Store the hashed values in a database.
 # Compare the values during the next import and generate QML components with unequal hash values.
 # Every time a QML component is edited, remove its hash.

This will only fly if the JSON created is stable. The JSON created by the plugin should be or can be made stable (By using stable ordered containers) but this JSON coming out of the design tool itself has to be checked.

summary: Analyse the model performance while importing Qt-Bridge archives
description:
Synthetic data Analysis. (macOS Instruments)
 * 20 % Parsing JSON (Actually 2% only, the rest is again ReadingContext calls from Model creation in Component class)
 * 80 % QML gen 
 ** 60 % Model Population (SyncNode 4% & ReadindContext 16%)
 ** 11 % QML file writing to disk (WriteAuxData takes the cake here also, ReadindContext stuff)
 ** 09 % Empty model creation (ReadindContext -> {color:#de350b}QMLJS:PopulateImportedTypes{color})

 

ReadingContext constructor ->QMLJS::LinkImports is the API that takes most of the time. SyncNode does take time but not as drastic)

summary: Have the icons of the Texture Bundle in the installer
description:
I have attached a zip with the icons for the "Texture Bundle" of the Content Library -- Textures and Environments.

Until now, if the user wanted to have textures in the Content Library, he had to download a big zip  (about 1.48 GB) of textures from a certain location, save it locally, e.g. in `C:\dev\texture_bundle` (so he would have directories `C:\dev\texture_bundle\Textures` and `C:\dev\texture_bundle\Environments`), and probably have some configuration done for Qt Design Studio to know to look into the `C:\dev\texture_bundle` folder for textures.

With the recent changes, the textures will be downloaded automatically from the internet by Qt Design Studio, but we currently still require to have the "icons" (i.e. thumbnails) available locally. We don't want the user to have to separately download these icons -- they are about 2MB in size, so they can safely be part of the Installer.

For example,

 * check error triaging on Tuesday
 * check testing status and need for fault fix confirmations on Wednesdays
 * check the documentation status on Thursdays
 * check the backlog on Fridays
 * etc..

Perhaps use some ready confluence page template for software development for tracking the project health status on weekly basis.

summary: Qt Safe Renderer plugins installation
description:
Currently, the problem is that Qt Safe Renderer does not work in QtCreator designer without building QSR from the sources and rebuilding the QML puppet. From the end-user point of view this is quite cumbersome and rebuilding QML Puppet is an unstable feature.

I have tested manually in Windows by extracting the following zip:

[http://ci-files02-hki.intra.qt.io/packages/jenkins/qtsaferenderer/1.2/latest/qtsaferenderer/|http://ci-files02-hki.intra.qt.io/packages/jenkins/qtsaferenderer/1.2/latest/qtsaferenderer/qtsaferenderer-Windows-Windows_10-MSVC2015-Windows-Windows_10-X86_64.7z] [qtsaferenderer-Windows-Windows_10-MSVC2015-Windows-Windows_10-X86_64.7z|http://ci-files02-hki.intra.qt.io/packages/jenkins/qtsaferenderer/1.2/latest/qtsaferenderer/qtsaferenderer-Windows-Windows_10-MSVC2015-Windows-Windows_10-X86_64.7z]

From that zip file SafeRenderer (from qml/Qt) folder, subfolders and files should be copied to the QtCreator binary folder: Tools\QtCreator\bin\qml\Qt

Then designer works flawlessly without rebuilding the puppet (and using the default Fallback QML emulation layer setting).

Similarly, we should add Linux and Mac dynamically build libraries to the ci-files and add those to the installer.

summary: PoC: The renderer should do alpha- blend to the background color
description:
It is possible to set the global background color to the StateManager.

Currently, it does not work as intended, because rendering rewrites the background with the alpha when rendering SafePicture or SafeText. Instead, it should do the alpha blending with the background color.

In addition, the background clearing should be moved from the StateManager and to the application responsibility.

Within that approach, it would be possible to make sure that text is always readable despite the non-safe UI on the background.

summary: Protect the data against accidental changes (e.g. read only states)
description:
Make sure that there won't be accidental changes.

E.g. set read-only property for the files in the sharepoint when those are approved. And have clear location for the branched versions.

The same applies to confluence pages. Maybe own space could be considered, where all have read-only data, but only the designated project members can edit the data. And after approval, change the page to read only state. (in case there is a need to update the page after the approval, it can still be done by removing the read only state temporarily)

summary: Use transparent clear color during animation
description:
If fillColor property is used on Safe Items, then the item is cleared by using the fillColor. This is however not compatible with animation as it would result in colored rectangles around the screen when the item is moved.

The solution seems to be to disable the fillColor during transition animation and use transparent clear color instead. The fillColor should then again be used, when the icon is at its destination.

Animation also makes the output verification impossible for moving items as the background layer behind safety layer shows up and makes it impossible to know the correct CRC of the area.

summary: POC: Create configuration file for the monitor
description:
Currently, the Golden CRC values are stored in the layout file.
Because monitor runs usually on the MCU which does have strict memory constraints it would be beneficial to have a separate configuration file that does not include unnecessary data.

There should be following data in the monitor configuration data:
Version number
ItemCount
ItemCount * 
[ ItemID
AssetID ]

AssetCount
AssetCount * [ AssetID
VisibleCRC
HiddenCRC ]

Optional:
StatesCount
StatesCount * [ StateName
TargetID
AssetID ]

summary: Streamline QSR build process for including layout data
description:
The current build process is a bit awkward. You have to run make once to generate layout data, then again to include the layout data in the qrc file.

Some feedback from a  customer:

I just wanted to provide a bit of feedback on the fix for the 'SafeRenderer::QSafeResource::ResourceException'   error.

The fix was to add the layout data to safeasset.qrc.
 It's a bit backwards because the layout files only get created by running make.

This means for any project you have to run make twice and add the newly created files to safeasset.qrc in between

In other words:
 # qmake
 # make
 # using qtcreator, right-click 'safeasset.qrc', select 'add existing files', select all files in 'layoutData'
 # make
 # after this the executable should work fine

Although this works, it certainly seems a bit odd. 
 At a minimum the run-time error should be augmented as I don't think I'll be the last to run into this.

description:
QSafeTextLayout::drawGlyph() algorithm depends on background being fully transparent (the default behaviour without fillColor) or fully opaque (when fillColor is used).

Make sure that tooling makes sure that the fillColor is fully opaque and make sure that Runtime checks and enforces this.

Tests needs to be implemented.

Also, see that opacity can be changed via state change (which should be possible and does not require Runtime to co-operate).

TestRail needs to be updated.

summary: Qt Safe Renderer 1.1 release
description:
Qt Safe Renderer 1.1 final release contains certified implementation of https://bugreports.qt.io/browse/QSR-257. 
This user story will contain all common sub-tasks that are required for creating and publishing the Qt Safe Renderer 1.1 final release and all its release candidates. 

* Testing:
for each release candidate there will be sub-tasks for different kind of legacy tests that are run for the release candidate (like "run legacy runtime tests on INTEGRITY for RC1"). The testing tasks for the new QSR 1.1 features are found under the related user story (QSR-257). Thus it is easy to see how many release candidates the QSR 1.1 release have had and what kind of tests (in high level) were executed for each release candidate.

* Documentation:
all general documentation sub-tasks (like writing the release note, verification report etc.) will be found under this user story. Documentation sub-tasks related to the new QSR 1.1 features (like updating the architecture specification) are found under the related user story (QSR-257).

This user story can be closed when QSR 1.1 final release has been published.

summary: Update QSR Safety plan for QSR 1.1
description:
QSR Safety plan needs to be updated for QSR release 1.1. 
Plan is available in Wiki: https://intranet.qt.io/display/QTRD/Qt+Safe+Renderer+Safety+Plan and if needed, it will be exported to .pdf.

All updates should be done in such a way that it is clear what is QSR 1.0 content, QSR 1.1 content and common content. For example, if you update the review policy:

Current version:

For the essential design documentation (system and unit design) inspection check lists must be used in reviews as requested by ISO 26262:2011 / ASIL-B.
    * Review approver has the responsibility to ensure checklists are fileld
    * Filled check list is to be stored to same Sharepoint folder with the document
    * Checklists shall be named using Qt_Safe_Renderer_<document name>_inspection_record as template

Updated version:

In QSR 1.0, for the essential design documentation (system and unit design) inspection check lists must be used in reviews as requested by ISO 26262:2011 / ASIL-B.
    * Review approver has the responsibility to ensure checklists are fileld
    * Filled check list is to be stored to same Sharepoint folder with the document
    * Checklists shall be named using Qt_Safe_Renderer_<document name>_inspection_record as template
In QSR 1.1, for the essential design documentation (system and unit design) inspection check lists must be used in reviews as requested by ISO 26262:2011 / ASIL-D.
    * <add the ASIL-D issues here>

* project organization for QSR 1.1
* Process tracking: in QSR 1.1, the documentation follow-up is done here: https://intranet.qt.io/display/QTRD/QSR+Release+1.1+Design+Phase+Verification (same page that contains the verification information too)
* Review policy - ASIL B --> ASIL-D
* requirement management: add QSR 1.1 tasks (for example, under own heading)
* release management: add link to QSR 1.1 items in on-line installer page (not yet done!), check if kanban link needs to be updated
* work products listed in the activity details table (chapter 4 in word document) could include also the concept status (part of architecture documentation); see QSR-216

summary: Safe renderer animation support
description:
I would like to be able to define Animations to Safe renderer objects where animation would be executed on non safe side and final place of the sefe item would be rendered again from safe side.

There should be a static analysis of animations and duration of the animation is defined at compile time to safe renderer. This makes sure that animation time is not exceeded dynamically. If animation is not yet completely done safe renderer will still render safe item after animation period.

This could also be used as nice demo where we first show nice animation flow and then dynamically make animation last longer so user is able to see that it's guaranteed that safe renderer will always render item after period defined in QML animation.

Need this to be driven by a customer with a real use case.
